title: Quote countdown restarts on every page load
summary: The quote page shows "Special online price ends in 09:59". Reloading the page restarts the timer at 10:00, so the deadline is not real.
rationale: Two reloads 90 seconds apart both showed 09:59 at first paint (FU-DC-1). No server deadline is returned by the quote API. The banner sits directly above the Buy now button, pressuring the customer to buy before comparing plans.

remediation.guidance: Remove the countdown, or drive it from a server-stored offer end time that is the same for every visitor and shown with its date and time in IST.

title: Countdown is seeded from a hard-coded 10-minute window
summary: QuoteTimer initialises its state to 600 seconds on mount. The deadline is created in the browser for each visit.
rationale: The timer value comes from useState(10 * 60) with no server input, which matches FU-SIG-CODE-1. This confirms the behaviour observed on the quote screen.

evidence.caption: Timer state initialised to 600 seconds on mount

remediation.guidance: Pass the offer end time from the pricing service and compute the remaining time from it; delete the local default.

title: "Only 3 policies left at this price" badge uses a random number
summary: A scarcity badge on the quote page shows between 2 and 4 policies remaining. Term insurance has no stock limit, and the number is random.
rationale: Policies are not a limited stock. The component generates the number with Math.random() (FU-DC-3), so the claim is fabricated.

evidence.caption: Scarcity badge next to the premium
Remaining count is random

remediation.guidance: Remove the scarcity badge. If a price is genuinely time-limited, state the end date instead.

title: Renewal push claims loyalty bonus is lost in 2 hours
summary: A renewal reminder says "Renew in the next 2 hours or lose your loyalty bonus". The policy is in its 30-day grace period and the bonus is not forfeited in 2 hours.
rationale: Policy terms keep loyalty additions until the end of the grace period. The 2-hour deadline has no basis and pushes an immediate renewal.

remediation.guidance: Replace the copy with the actual grace period end date and what happens after it.

title: Critical Illness Rider is pre-selected in the proposal form
summary: The cover options step shows the Critical Illness Rider already ticked, adding ₹312 a month to the premium unless the customer unticks it.
rationale: The rider is optional and priced separately. It is included by default (BS-SIG-SCR-1) and raises the premium from ₹1,184 to ₹1,496 a month without an affirmative choice by the customer.

remediation.guidance: Default all riders to unselected and show each rider’s premium next to its checkbox.

title: Proposal state defaults criticalIllnessRider to true
summary: The initial cover options object sets criticalIllnessRider: true, which renders the rider as selected for every customer.
rationale: Matches BS-DC-2: an optional rider initialised to true in client state.

evidence.caption: Optional rider initialised to selected

remediation.guidance: Set every rider to false in the initial state and add a unit test asserting no paid option is preselected.

title: Proposal API adds the Critical Illness Rider when no riders are sent
summary: ProposalService attaches the Critical Illness Rider when a channel omits the rider list, so partner and assisted channels also sell the rider by default.
rationale: Server-side defaulting (BS-SIG-BE-1) means removing the web preselection alone would not fix other channels.

evidence.caption: Rider added when the request has no riders

remediation.guidance: Treat a missing rider list as no riders. Reject ambiguous requests instead of defaulting.

title: Premium Protection Plan pre-selected at renewal
summary: The app renewal checkout includes a ticked "Premium Protection Plan ₹199/year" that the customer did not add.
rationale: An optional paid plan is pre-selected and included in the renewal total.

remediation.guidance: Show the plan as an unticked option with its price.

title: Decline link reads "No, I don't care about my family's future"
summary: The only way to leave the quote without buying is a link that implies the customer does not care about their family.
rationale: The wording attributes a negative motive to declining (CS-C-1) on a purchase decision (CS-C-2).

evidence.caption: Buy now button and decline link

remediation.guidance: Replace with a neutral option such as "Not now" or "Compare other plans".

title: Renewal decline link: "No, I'll risk losing my cover"
summary: The link to leave the renewal checkout frames declining as reckless.
rationale: Guilt-inducing wording on a renewal decision. The customer may intend to renew later or through another channel.

remediation.guidance: Use "Renew later" and show the grace period end date.

title: Add-on decline copy flagged for review
summary: The lexicon check flagged the add-on decline strings. On review the wording is neutral.
rationale: "Maybe later" with a factual hint does not attribute a negative motive to the customer.

evidence.content:
"payment.addons.decline": "Maybe later",
  "payment.addons.declineHint": "You can add cover any time from My Policies",
evidence.caption: Decline strings for the add-on offer

remediation.guidance: No change needed.

title: Website grievance page requires installing the mobile app
summary: Visitors who open "Raise a grievance" on the website see only a prompt to download the app. There is no web form, e-mail address or other alternative on the page.
rationale: Access to grievance redressal is blocked behind an unrelated action (installing an app) with no alternative path, which meets the critical severity rule.

remediation.guidance: Restore a web grievance form and list e-mail, phone and branch options on the page.

title: Grievance route redirects non-app users to /get-app
summary: GrievancePage redirects any visitor without an app session to the app download page.
rationale: Route guard enforcing an unrelated action (FA-SIG-CODE-1).

evidence.caption: Redirect for visitors without an app session

remediation.guidance: Remove the guard and render GrievanceForm for all visitors.

title: Claim intimation requires agreeing to promotional offers
summary: The claim form cannot be submitted unless the claimant ticks "I agree to receive promotional offers from Example Life and partners".
rationale: Marketing consent is unrelated to intimating a claim and is marked as required.

remediation.guidance: Make marketing consent optional and separate from claim submission.

title: App requests contacts and precise location during proposal
summary: The Android app declares READ_CONTACTS and ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION and requests them on the nominee step of the proposal.
rationale: Neither permission is needed to add a nominee. Whether progress is blocked when refused needs confirming in the journey.

remediation.guidance: Remove READ_CONTACTS and ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, or make them optional with a manual entry fallback.

title: Auto-debit cancellation ends in "visit a branch or call us"
summary: After five screens, the final step of cancelling the premium auto-debit tells the customer to visit a branch or call during office hours. Setting up the mandate took two taps in the app.
rationale: Cancellation needs an offline channel while sign-up was online, and takes far more steps (ST-C-1, ST-C-4). This meets the critical severity rule.

remediation.guidance: Add a self-service "Cancel auto-debit" action in the app that completes the cancellation.

title: Payments API has no mandate cancellation operation
summary: The payments API exposes create and get operations for mandates but no cancel operation, so no channel can offer self-service cancellation.
rationale: Creation is self-service while cancellation is not (ST-SIG-BE-1). This is the root cause of the app behaviour.

evidence.content:
/v1/mandates:
    post:
      summary: Register an e-mandate for premium auto-debit
      operationId: createMandate
  /v1/mandates/{mandateId}:
    get:
      summary: Get mandate status
      operationId: getMandate
    # No self-service cancel operation; cancellations are raised by branch staff
evidence.caption: Mandate operations in the payments API

remediation.guidance: Add a cancel operation that revokes the mandate with the sponsor bank and confirms to the customer.

title: Turning off auto-renewal passes through three retention screens
summary: Switching off auto-renewal pushes a retention offer, a mandatory survey and an OTP plus callback confirmation. Switching it on is a single toggle.
rationale: Cancel flow with multiple mandatory retention screens (ST-SIG-CODE-2).

evidence.caption: Auto-renewal off flow

remediation.guidance: Allow one dismissible retention offer, make the survey optional and remove the callback requirement.

title: Add-on modal: large "Continue with add-ons" versus faint "Skip"
summary: The add-on offer before payment has a full-width primary button to accept and an 11px light-grey "Skip" link to decline.
rationale: Measured contrast of "Skip" is 1.6:1 against white and the accept button area is about 40 times larger (II-DC-1).

remediation.guidance: Show "Continue without add-ons" as a secondary button of similar size and AA contrast.

title: Skip link styled text-[11px] text-slate-300
summary: The decline control in AddOnModal used an 11px, slate-300 style that fails contrast requirements.
rationale: Low-contrast styling of the decline option (II-SIG-CODE-1). Fixed in release 2026.09.2; retest passed.

evidence.code:
<Button size="lg" className="w-full" onClick={acceptAddOns}>
        Continue with add-ons (+₹{addOnTotal}/month)
      </Button>
      <button className="mt-3 text-[11px] text-slate-300" onClick={skip}>
        Skip
      </button>
evidence.caption: Decline control styling (before fix)

remediation.guidance: Use the secondary button variant for the decline option.

title: Home page hero emphasises "Get a quote"
summary: The visual heuristic flagged the prominent hero button. There is no competing choice on the hero, so this is ordinary visual hierarchy.
rationale: A single primary action with no hidden alternative falls under the exclusion for normal hierarchy.

remediation.guidance: No change needed.

title: Advertised ₹649/month becomes ₹1,184/month on the quote
summary: The home page promises ₹1 crore cover "from ₹649/month". A 34-year-old non-smoker is quoted ₹1,184, and the quote page does not explain the difference.
rationale: The advertised price is not shown with a reference profile, and the quote gives no reasons for the difference.

remediation.guidance: State the reference profile for the headline price and explain the factors behind each quote.

title: Headline premium is below the minimum monthly premium
summary: The rating rules set a minimum monthly premium of ₹812, but the marketing headline uses ₹649. No customer can obtain the advertised price.
rationale: The advertised outcome is unattainable for any profile (BW-DC-2), which meets the critical severity rule.

evidence.content:
product: EXAMPLE_SECURE_TERM_PLUS
base_rate_per_lakh:
  age_18_25: 7.40
  age_26_35: 9.10
  age_36_45: 14.80
minimum_monthly_premium: 812
marketing:
  headline_premium: 649   # used on home page banner
evidence.caption: Rating rules for the term plan

remediation.guidance: Generate the headline premium from the rating engine for a stated reference profile.

title: "Policy administration fee" appears only on the payment page
summary: A ₹299 policy administration fee first appears in the payment summary. It was not shown on the quote, proposal or add-on screens.
rationale: A mandatory fee revealed at the final step (DP-C-1) makes the total payable higher than the quoted amount (DP-C-2).

remediation.guidance: Show the fee in the first quoted total, or remove it.

title: Pricing rule adds a fee only at the payment step
summary: The POLICY_ADMIN_FEE rule applies only when journey_step is payment and is hidden from quotes. PremiumCalculator adds fees per step.
rationale: Step-conditioned fee (DP-DC-2) confirmed in both configuration and code, so the amount charged exceeds what the customer confirmed.

evidence.content:
- id: POLICY_ADMIN_FEE
    description: Policy administration fee
    amount: 299
    apply_when:
      journey_step: payment
      channel: web
    display_on_quote: false
evidence.caption: Fee rule conditioned on the payment step
Fees applied per journey step

remediation.guidance: Remove step conditions from fee rules and assert in tests that the payment amount equals the confirmed quote.

title: Monthly renewal quote omits modal loading
summary: The renewal quote divides the annual premium by 12. Monthly-mode loading is added later at payment.
rationale: The displayed monthly premium is lower than the amount collected.

evidence.caption: Renewal quote calculation

remediation.guidance: Include modal loading in the displayed renewal premium.

title: "Top rated plans" ranks partner plans first without a sponsored label
summary: The home page section "Top rated plans for you" puts two partner plans from Sample General Assurance above Example Life's own plan. Nothing indicates that the order is commercially weighted.
rationale: The ranking is presented as editorial (DA-C-2) and has no disclosure (DA-C-3). The ranking configuration confirms partner weighting (DA-C-1).

boxes.label: Partner plans ranked #1 and #2 with no sponsored label

remediation.guidance: Label partner placements as sponsored, or rank by customer-relevant criteria only.

title: Ranking score weights partner boost equally with rating
summary: The catalogue ranking gives partner_boost the same weight as customer rating and disables the sponsored label.
rationale: Commercial weighting in ranking configuration (DA-DC-2).

evidence.content:
ranking:
  label: "Top rated plans"
  score: "0.5 * customer_rating + 0.5 * partner_boost"
  partner_boost:
    SAMPLE_GENERAL_WEALTH_SHIELD: 1.0
    SAMPLE_GENERAL_SMART_SAVER: 0.9
    EXAMPLE_SECURE_TERM_PLUS: 0.2
  show_sponsored_label: false
evidence.caption: Catalogue ranking configuration

remediation.guidance: Set show_sponsored_label to true and publish the ranking basis.

title: Renewal reminder scheduler has no frequency cap
summary: The renewal_reminder job runs every two hours from 8 AM to 8 PM across push, SMS and WhatsApp, with no daily cap, quiet hours or opt-out check.
rationale: Scheduler with no frequency cap (NG-DC-1). ReminderJob sends on every channel without checking preferences, so opting out does not stop it (NG-C-3).

evidence.content:
jobs:
  renewal_reminder:
    schedule: "0 0 8-20/2 * * *"   # every 2 hours, 8 AM to 8 PM
    channels: [push, sms, whatsapp]
    audience: policies_due_within_30_days
    stop_when: renewed
    # max_per_day: not configured
    # quiet_hours: not configured
evidence.caption: Renewal reminder job
Reminder job sends on every channel

remediation.guidance: Cap renewal reminders at one per day per channel, add quiet hours, and check communication preferences before sending.

title: Six renewal reminders received in one day
summary: During the 24-hour observation window the test device received six renewal push notifications, every two hours from 8 AM to 6 PM.
rationale: Repeated identical requests (NG-C-1) observed in the journey, consistent with the scheduler configuration.

remediation.guidance: Apply the scheduler cap and verify with a 24-hour retest.

title: Top-up cover sheet appears on every app launch
summary: A cross-sell sheet for Top-Up Health Cover opens every time the app is launched. The only dismissal is "Remind me later".
rationale: Repeated prompt unrelated to the servicing task, with no lasting way to stop it.

remediation.guidance: Show at most once every 30 days and add "Don't show again".

title: HomeActivity shows the cross-sell sheet in onResume without a dismissal check
summary: The sheet is shown whenever the customer lacks top-up cover, on every resume, with no persisted dismissal.
rationale: Prompt trigger without a persisted dismissal flag (NG-SIG-CODE-1).

evidence.caption: Cross-sell trigger

remediation.guidance: Persist dismissal server-side and throttle the prompt.

title: Partner offers consent uses a double negative
summary: The proposal form asks the customer to "Untick this box if you do not wish to not receive offers from our partners". The box is ticked by default.
rationale: A double negative in a data-sharing consent (TQ-C-1) makes it likely the customer consents without meaning to (TQ-C-2).

evidence.caption: Consent section of the proposal form

remediation.guidance: Rewrite as "Share my details with partners for offers", unticked by default.

title: Preference toggles: "Don't stop sending me offers"
summary: Communication preferences use reversed labels such as "Don't stop sending me offers" and "Opt out of not receiving renewal tips", all switched on.
rationale: Reversed and double-negative toggle labels on the consent withdrawal screen.

remediation.guidance: Use positive labels ("Send me offers by SMS") and default them to off.

title: Consent stored as marketing_opt_out with inverted meaning
summary: The consent table stores marketing_opt_out (default true) while the app label means "keep sending". Reports and exports may read the flag the wrong way round.
rationale: Consent stored with semantics inverted relative to the UI label (TQ-SIG-BE-1).

evidence.content:
CREATE TABLE customer_consent (
  customer_id       BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
  -- UI label: "Don't stop sending me offers" (toggle ON = true)
  marketing_opt_out BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  partner_sharing   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
  updated_at        TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
evidence.caption: Consent table definition

remediation.guidance: Rename to marketing_consent with the same meaning as the UI label and migrate existing values.

title: Wellness Plus trial converts to ₹99/month without reminders
summary: The Wellness Plus add-on requires an e-mandate for its 30-day trial and converts to paid with trial-ending and pre-debit notifications switched off.
rationale: Silent trial conversion (SB-C-2) and recurring debit without prior notice (SB-C-1).

evidence.content:
wellness_plus:
  trial_days: 30
  price_monthly: 99
  convert_on_trial_end: true
  mandate_required_for_trial: true
  notifications:
    trial_ending: false
    pre_debit: false
evidence.caption: Wellness Plus subscription configuration

remediation.guidance: Enable trial-ending and pre-debit notifications and ask for explicit confirmation before conversion.

title: Premium auto-debit flagged as recurring billing
summary: The recurring premium debit was flagged by the recurring-billing check. Pre-debit notices are sent 48 hours ahead.
rationale: Recurring premiums for a policy the customer knowingly bought, with pre-debit notices, fall under the exclusion.

evidence.content:
premium_autodebit:
  mandate_type: e_mandate
  pre_debit_notification_hours: 48
  channels: [sms, email]
evidence.caption: Premium auto-debit configuration

remediation.guidance: No change needed.

title: Third-party SDK flagged by the risk scan
summary: The SDK inventory flagged an unfamiliar SDK. Review found it is an analytics library that does not show ads or install packages.
rationale: No scare messaging or install prompts; the SDK is not on the known adware list.

evidence.content:
sdks:
  - name: sample-analytics-sdk
    version: 3.4.1
    category: analytics
    shows_ads: false
    requests_install_packages: false
evidence.caption: SDK inventory entry

remediation.guidance: No change needed. Keep the SDK inventory in the release checklist.

title: "Price held for 10:00" timer on the payment page
summary: The payment page showed a 10-minute price hold timer that did not correspond to any server-side hold. Removed in release 2026.09.1.
rationale: Unverifiable urgency on the payment step. Retest on 15 September 2026 confirmed the timer is gone.

remediation.guidance: Removed. Keep a regression check in the payment page tests.

title: Grievance page link: "I'd rather complain than read FAQs"
summary: The link to continue to the complaint path mocked customers who skip the FAQs. The copy was replaced with "Continue to raise a grievance".
rationale: Ridicule attached to the complaint path. Remediated and retested.

remediation.guidance: Replaced with neutral copy.

title: "Save draft" is a faint text link next to a large "Submit claim"
summary: The claim form gives a small grey "Save draft" link beside the primary button, so claimants may submit incomplete claims.
rationale: Unequal prominence between two relevant choices on the claim form.

remediation.guidance: Show "Save draft" as a secondary button.

title: "Loyalty price ends in 04:59" countdown on renewal
summary: The redesigned renewal screen opens with a five-minute countdown for a "loyalty price".
rationale: Countdown on a renewal decision with no deadline in the renewal API.

remediation.guidance: Remove the countdown before release.

title: Renewal Shield add-on pre-selected
summary: "Renewal Shield ₹349/year" is ticked by default on the new renewal screen.
rationale: Optional paid add-on included by default.

remediation.guidance: Default the add-on to unselected.

title: Decline link "No, I'll pay more later"
summary: Leaving the renewal offer uses a link that implies the customer is choosing to overpay.
rationale: Loaded decline wording on a renewal decision.

remediation.guidance: Use "Not now".

title: Convenience fee appears on the final payment screen
summary: A ₹49 convenience fee is added on the payment screen and was not shown on the renewal offer.
rationale: Mandatory fee revealed at the last step.

remediation.guidance: Show the fee on the renewal offer total.

title: "Pay with AutoPay" dominates "Pay once"
summary: AutoPay is a large primary button and one-time payment is a small grey link.
rationale: Unequal prominence steering customers into a recurring mandate.

remediation.guidance: Offer both options as equal buttons.

title: "Uncheck to not opt out of AutoPay reminders"
summary: A pre-ticked checkbox on the payment screen uses a double negative.
rationale: Confusing consent wording.

remediation.guidance: Rephrase positively and leave unticked.
